parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime pairs one of the friendlier state/province layers with a sharply hostile national layer the traveller cannot avoid. Entry is a tier-1 universal exposure: passports now record sex assigned at birth, X markers are discontinued, secondary scrutiny and a visa-fraud cable target document/presentation mismatch, and travellers report confiscation and stranding. National custody (immigration detention, corrections policy) documents severe harm. Within the jurisdiction itself, facilities are protected, discrimination remedies operate, care is lawful, and a documented risk assessment places it in the low-risk tier; no hate-crime statute and a youth-sports bill are modest open questions. A trans adult can visit safely if uneventful, but any national-system encounter (border, detention, federal facility) carries real exposure. Minors face additional national hostility (care framing, school directives), though local care is lawful. Net: elevated-to-reduced boundary.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports/visas record birth sex; X markers discontinued; visa cable directs refusal on reasonable doubt about sex and flags lifetime fraud findings; travellers report confiscated passports and stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Passport policy remains in litigation; existing X passports valid; external governments issue advisories and a legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: National screening precedes any state-province experience; the exposure is inescapable at entry regardless of local protections.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy removes hormones and mandates forced conformity for trans inmates; immigration custody documented with forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner counts.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest or immigration issue routes the visitor into the national custody regime, bypassing state-level protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Nationally funded single-sex facilities exclude trans people per January 2025 order; ~21 states have facility bans, 4 criminalise in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This jurisdiction has no facility ban, requires gender-neutral restrooms in public buildings, and bans discrimination; the local trespass statute does not apply here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility access is state-governed; within this jurisdiction access is congruent, though any national facility follows the exclusion rule.

care_services.exposure: National orders frame minor care as 'mutilation', proposed insurance bars, hospital-record subpoenas; the parent framework burdens travelling minors' care.
care_services.protection: Gender-affirming care lawful statewide; largest city is a documented sanctuary shielding travellers from external enforcement; remedies via human relations commission operate.
care_services.interaction: State sanctuary practice interacts with and partially shields against national-level enforcement for care sought locally.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National rhetoric ('radical gender ideology', counterterrorism prioritisation of 'radically pro-transgender' groups), athlete-entry ban, state flag prohibition signals hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Local police operate under binding regulations defining sex to include gender identity; commission remedies enforceable.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National reward/counterterrorism framing is aimed at advocacy, not visitors per se, but raises discovery-consequence stakes.

minors_guardians.exposure: National EO directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating a minor's transition; 27 states ban youth care; national athlete-entry ban; parent/guardian of a trans minor faces documentation mismatch and surveillance of school-related support.
minors_guardians.protection: Local ordinances bar youth-serving discrimination; X markers on virtual school records; conversion-therapy bans locally.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor is safe locally but exposed in any national-system contact (schools funded federally, border, healthcare records).

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide hate-crime statute reaching anti-LGBTQ violence (2008 striking down, reinstatement failed); national bias-crime coverage partial.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; local anti-discrimination enforcement documented and functioning; statewide risk assessment places jurisdiction in low-risk tier.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police response supported by regulation; remedy gap exists if bias-motivated violence occurs.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Recurring national litigation unresolved; equality statute not yet passed (commission interpretation only); sports bills repeatedly advanced; national trajectory degrading.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working local complaint system; sanctuary order; national courts have enjoined some orders and the passport suit is live.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Practical exposure depends on which national measures are operative at travel time; protections are regulatory, not statutory, and thus reversible.

anchor_checks.comparison: Comparable on the local layer: brief friction with working remedies, no imprisonment locally. But this jurisdiction's national layer adds a universal document/entry exposure (birth-sex passports, visa-fraud cable) that 0.65-A's regime lacks, pulling the combined regime below that anchor.

The national border screening here is more structured and consequential than 0.55-B's discretionary secondary checks — refusals, case-note tagging, and lifetime fraud findings are codified, and custody harms are documented. This regime is worse than 0.55-B at entry, better in daily life.

0.75-C features brief detention with functioning appeals and no custody-abuse pattern. This jurisdiction's documented national detention abuses (forced labour, sexual violence) and criminalised trespass in sister states sit materially below 0.75-C, while local protections roughly match its remedies layer.

0.45-D imposes universal registration exposing every visitor. This jurisdiction lacks such a local regime, but the national passport/visa regime is a partial analogue at the border only, not in daily life — so it sits clearly above 0.45-D.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller experiences two regimes in sequence. At entry and in any national-system contact (custody, federal facilities, records), the parent framework imposes universal, documented exposure: birth-sex documents, fraud-based refusals, and custodial practices with severe documented harm — tier-1/tier-2 features. Within the jurisdiction, the operative regime is protective: explicit discrimination coverage with functioning remedies, facility access congruent with identity, lawful care with a documented sanctuary for travellers, and a third-party low-risk grading. The harshest operative rule governs the visit's most dangerous moments, but daily life in the jurisdiction resembles the 0.65–0.75 tier. Combining: strong local protections do not cancel national border and custody exposure; recurring unremedied national custody violations and partial recourse hold the score in the upper Elevated Risk band.
